title: Elven Realms - A Fantasy Music Pack - 44 Tracks
tagline: 44 track elven fantasy score in two modes: canopy city, deep wood, high court, the old war. MIDI + looping OGG.
description:
Elven Realms is a 44 track high fantasy score for games: a city in the canopy of a great forest, its court and its glades, the deep wood and the old roads, the barrows of the first kings, and the old war that comes back to the border, with seven pieces for it from the first memory to the final boss.

Two modes, one realm, checked on the shipped MIDI. Every track is in one of two modes: 22 in Lydian, the bright mode with a raised fourth, for the light, the court and the glade; 22 in Dorian, the minor mode with a raised sixth, for the wood, the barrows and the war. Each mode has one note that makes it itself rather than plain major or minor, and the lead line of every one of the 44 tracks sounds it: 397 colour notes across the leads, at least 2 in each. We ran the same check over our 23 other albums: 183 of their 905 tracks pass it, and none of the albums passes it on every track.

What is in it. 34 full pieces and 10 short cues, 46:12 of music. The light: The Elder Light, Aelindar, the Canopy City, Aelindar at Night, The Moonlit Glade, The Glade Before Dawn, The High Court, The Council of Leaves, The Queen's Garden, The Star Archive, The Bowyer's Hall, The Moonwell and The Leaf and Lantern. The wood and the wild: The Leafways, The Deepwood, The Deepwood After Dark, The Silver River, The Falls of Morning, The Border Road, The Barrow of the First Kings, The Root Caverns, The Starlit Pass and The Western Shore. The old war: The Old War, A Shadow at the Border, Battle in the Boughs, The Thornguard, The Warden of Thorns, The Hollow King and The Last Defence. After: Under the Same Stars, Lament for the Fallen, The Crowning of the Spring, The Long Farewell and A Song for the Stars. Cues: A Path Revealed, Gift of the Wood, Steel Among the Leaves, The Thorns Fall, The Light Dims, Grown Taller, A Task from the Court, The Moonwell's Blessing, A Word of Old Speech and The Hidden Door.

What you get. 44 OGG files, 34 of them with sample accurate LOOPSTART and LOOPLENGTH tags, which is what RPG Maker MV and MZ read. 44 editable .mid sources. A Readme with per engine import notes, both proof reports, and a royalty free commercial licence.

One family of five cells from one seed. Leaf, Bough, Star, Root and Thorn. Leaf is the realm: it steps up, reaches a third and lands a fourth higher. Bough is Leaf turned over and carries the deep wood and the night. Star opens Leaf out to a fifth for wonder and the sky. Root pulls it in to steps for travel and work. Thorn falls and climbs back, and every fight opens on it. 1864 statements and fragments of those cells across the album, counted by the harness in the finished MIDI.

Gate results. 780 theory checks and 498 audio checks, 0 failed, and both reports ship inside the download. They say the music is correctly written, rendered and tagged. They are not a claim about taste, which is what the free tracks are for.

Two full tracks are free on this page, with their MIDI: The Elder Light, the title theme in Lydian, and The Warden of Thorns, the boss in Dorian, so you can hear both modes before you buy.

The renders are a General MIDI reference render through a conventional soundfont. The composition system is AI written code and no generative audio model is used anywhere.

devlog.title: Elven Realms is out: a 44 track fantasy score in two modes
devlog.body:
Elven Realms is a 44 track high fantasy score for games: a canopy city and its court, glades, a deep wood, old roads and barrows, and the old war at the border with its battles and two bosses. It is live now, with two full tracks free to download from the page.

The idea. Fantasy scores often reach for the same major and minor keys as everything else. This one holds two modes across the whole record: Lydian, with its raised fourth, for the light, and Dorian, with its raised sixth, for the wood and the war. The lead line of every track sounds its mode's colour note, 397 times across the album, checked on the shipped MIDI. None of our 23 earlier albums passes that check on every track.

How it was checked. 780 theory checks and 498 audio checks, 0 failed, with both reports inside the download. Those numbers say the music is correctly written, rendered and tagged. They are not a claim about taste, which is what the free pair (The Elder Light and The Warden of Thorns) is for.

The renders are a General MIDI reference render through a conventional soundfont. The composition system is AI written code and no generative audio model is used.
